anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet the barrel jack J2 is wired so that the BAT+ rail (NET0008, the node that also carries USB VBUS from J9.1 and IC2 VIN/EN) is tied to one of the jack's switch pins (the pin the in-schematic note calls '2 and 3 are shorted with no plug'), the battery-negative node NET0034 (U9 cathode / U8 minus) is tied to the remaining jack pins, and the GND symbol is attached to the jack's left-side mounting terminal (MH1) rather than to the sleeve pin. The result is that pin 1 (which the note states is the center/positive) is not on BAT+ and pin 2 (sleeve) is not on GND.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the jack must be wired J4.1->BAT+ (center/positive), J4.2->GND (sleeve), J4.3->BAT-, so that with no plug the 2-3 short ties the battery return (BAT-) to GND and inserting a DC plug breaks that short to disconnect the battery, while the adapter's center-positive feeds BAT+ and its sleeve feeds GND.

evidence.quote: Netlist: J4.1->BAT+ (center/positive), J4.2->GND (sleeve), J4.3->BAT-. Since pins 2 and 3 are normally shorted (per the note) ... the jack's internal switch keeps the battery's return path connected to GND by default, and inserting a DC plug breaks that short - disconnecting the battery.

anomalies.impact: The DC-input summation is miswired: the adapter sleeve/center are not on GND/BAT+ respectively, so plugging in a barrel adapter can short the adapter ground to BAT+ and/or apply reverse polarity across the 18650 cell (the documented 'shorts battery' failure), and the battery-disconnect-by-jack function is lost (battery return is not switched to GND).

parsed.summary: All component types, values and the EPD/Skylab/regulator topologies match the specification, but the DC barrel jack J2 on the power sheet is wired contrary to the spec's explicit pin1->BAT+/pin2->GND/pin3->BAT- mapping (BAT+ on a switch pin, GND on a mounting terminal, battery-negative on the center), which reintroduces the documented 'DC plug pins are wrong, shorts battery' condition.
